summary: The clearest format criticism in the corpus sits in this thread: a well-liked comment argues the game is rigged by design because every question is one a celebrity could be sued for answering, so nobody was ever going to answer and the whole thing collapses into forced eating — the fix suggested is a wider spread of questions that can actually be answered. Around that, the reaction is warm: the guest is funny, unpretentious, and viewers want her back regularly. The top comment is a crossover request pairing the hosts with a comedy creator. One viewer catches a continuity error where a question is skipped in the edit. A sponsor link for an international skincare device sits in the hosts' own pinned comment.

themes.label: The question design makes the game fake
themes.example: คำถามก็คือไม่มีใครกล้าตอบอยู่แล้ว เพราะ ... ยังไงก็เสี่ยงโดนฟ้อง ... เอาจริงๆน่าจะกระจายๆคำถามที่ตอบได้มาเยอะกว่านี้หน่อย

themes.label: The guest's comedic side
themes.example: พี่ใหม่น่ารักอะ ตลกมากกกกก ฮาา ขอพี่ใหม่มาเรื่อยๆเลยค้าบบบบ

themes.label: Crossover requests with other creators
themes.example: อยากเห็นพวกเจ๊ ไป join กับ เทพลีลา ดู อยากเห็นมากเลย

themes.label: Editing continuity error caught
themes.example: จริงๆพี่ดรีมต้องตอบอีกคำถามนะ มีช็อตที่ข้ามไปพี่ใหม่เลย

themes.label: Sponsor placement in the pinned comment
themes.example: เพราะเรามาส์กหน้าด้วย #FOREOUFO2 ค่า

audience_signals: The audience will diagnose a broken format mechanic precisely and propose the fix — here, that legally risky questions guarantee refusal and turn a choice game into a gag; this is the single most actionable production note in the set
Viewers catch continuity errors in the edit, so post-production sloppiness is visible to them
The channel carries international brand sponsorship (a skincare device) as well as its own products, which broadens the commercial picture
Crossover requests name creators outside the celebrity circuit, suggesting appetite for creator-versus-creator formats the channel has not tried
content_requests: Mix in questions guests can actually answer
